justification: Changes which rules the live assessment page shows for every lot on a flood map, the bushfire-prone map, the acid sulfate map or riparian land, and for heritage properties with any of those. Today every condition-layer rule reaches no house because the page never sends the facts.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured live 2026-10-11: 18 Castra Pl Double Bay and 44 Victoria St Paddington carry dcpFloodMap.inFloodArea=true in /api/property, yet the page's request has no flood param and shows 0 of 44 Woollahra E2.3 flood rules. Served condition rows: flood 44, heritage 394, none 411 (the latter two reach heritage houses through the heritage branch).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I had moved Woollahra E2.3 into the condition layer assuming the page sends flood; it never did (buildForPropertyParams had no flood/bushfire), so 4 rules previously shown to every house became hidden too. The route's heritage branch also returned heritage rules only, so a heritage house never saw its condition rules. /api/property/profile returns a short summary, but the page's rule facts come from /api/property via usePropertyAssessment.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new module: extends the existing query builder, the route's existing condition filter, and the existing gate-rule list.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The facts come from /api/property (Planning Portal layerintersect plus spatial_overlays). When that lookup fails the page sends no facts, and the condition layer shows nothing -- the same visible-absence state as before, not a wrong rule.
pre_impl.frontend_type: New optional boolean inputs on ForPropertyQueryInput; the call site passes strict === true comparisons and Boolean(acidSulfateSoils), so undefined/null never becomes 'true'.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Silent omission today: flood, bushfire, acid sulfate and riparian rules never appear. After this, a wrong flag would show or hide those rules for a lot; the flags are the Portal's and spatial_overlays' own, and the live checks after deploy must show a flood house getting E2.3 and a dry house not.

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/dcp-provisions-query.test.ts ; python -m pytest tests/test_gate_rules.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The jest test fails if flood/bushfire/acid_sulfate/riparian are sent when not true, not sent when true, or if the mounted component stops passing the flood map and bushfire flag. The pytest suite fails if DQ-146 stops counting the new condition names as reachable or a gate rule touches a non-gate column.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Live before the change: flood-map houses shown 0 of 44 flood rules. Jest could not run locally (the main checkout's node_modules is incomplete); CI runs it. Python: 46 passed.

functions.name: buildForPropertyParams
functions.input: the page's former council, zone, heritage, outline ids, land facts and site-condition booleans
functions.output: The query string for /api/provisions/for-property, with each site condition present only when true
functions.if_none: An absent or null condition sends nothing, and the route treats it as not on that map.

values.what: Woollahra E2.3 flood rules shown to a lot on Woollahra's Flood Planning Area map
values.source: live capture of 18 Castra Place Double Bay via /api/property then /api/provisions/for-property
values.if_missing: A failed property lookup is reported as such and not counted.

queries.purpose: Serve condition-layer rules only for conditions the lot has.
queries.where_clause: v2_dcp_layer = 'condition' AND v2_site_condition_required = ANY(flood|bushfire|acid_sulfate|riparian, only those sent true)

break_it.scenario: A heritage house that is also on a flood map asks for its rules.
break_it.what_happens: Before: only heritage rules came back from the condition layer.
break_it.how: The heritage branch now merges heritage rows with the condition rows for the lot's conditions, de-duplicated by id.

break_it.scenario: The property lookup fails and returns no constraints for the lot.
break_it.what_happens: No site-condition flags are sent, so no condition rules are shown for it.
break_it.how: Strict === true comparisons; nothing is sent, the condition layer returns none -- an omission, not a wrong rule; the lookup-failure fault is tracked separately.
break_it.repro: jest test 'sends flood and bushfire only when true'

break_it.scenario: The gate-rule write runs before the page change deploys.
break_it.what_happens: Rules moved to the condition layer would be hidden from every house until deploy.
break_it.how: apply_site_condition_gates.sh says to run after deploy; the write is sequenced after merge and deploy.

break_it.scenario: acidSulfateSoils holds a class string for every lot, including off-map lots.
break_it.what_happens: Acid sulfate rules would then reach every lot in the council, including dry ones.
break_it.how: It is set only when the Acid Sulfate Soils Map layer intersects the lot (nsw-planning-portal.ts) or the PostGIS acid_sulfate overlay matches; absent otherwise.

break_it.scenario: Querying condition rules with an empty conditions array.
break_it.what_happens: ANY('{}') would return nothing, which is correct, but a code path that skipped the empty check could error.
break_it.how: The existing early return when no condition is sent is kept.

post_merge.db_reset: Yes, after deploy, user-approved ('go with your recommendation'): bash scripts/apply_site_condition_gates.sh (25 rows; backups first).
post_merge.manual_verify: Live checks after deploy: a flood-map house shows E2.3 flood rules, a dry house shows none; a Ku-ring-gai bushfire-prone house shows Part 16. Jest runs in CI only (local node_modules incomplete).
